description: Each quiz item corresponds to one row of File 1.
Shuffle the four options at quiz time and grade by option text, never by letter, to eliminate source answer-position bias.
Accept given numeric answer if absolute error <= max(0.01, 1% of correct); strip trailing %, commas, and spaces. For percent hint, input raw number.
Compare execution result sets on sample database from stem tables ignoring aliases and unrequested row order; fallback to LLM judge if sandbox unavailable. All-or-nothing (1 or 0).
Display the pedagogical explanation from the source immediately after each submitted question.
Takes a list of skills (or categories expanding to skills) and the hardest claimed difficulty (1=Easy, 2=Medium, 3=Hard).
Calibrate quiz length based on count of declared skills (10, 12, 14, or 15 questions).
Allocate 75% questions to declared skills and 25% (min 2) to undeclared related skills (STRONG first, difficulty level minus 1, min 1).
Difficulty breakdown based on claim: Easy (80/20/0), Medium (20/60/20), Hard (0/30/70 with stretch probes).
At least 1 question per declared skill when count <= 70% of quiz length; otherwise sample without replacement prioritizing earliest phases.
For declared skills with >= 2 questions: CONFIRMED (>=70%), PARTIAL (50-69%), NOT_CONFIRMED (<50%). If < 2 questions, rollup to category and mark indicative.
Overall assessment verdict on declared skills at claimed difficulty: Confirmed (>=70%), Partially confirmed (50-69%), Not confirmed (<50%).
Skip or lightly revise CONFIRMED skills; schedule PARTIAL, NOT_CONFIRMED, undeclared related skills scoring <60%, and undeclared skills, weak first.
Offer quiz immediately when learner completes skills in trigger_after_skill_ids or entire phase.
>=70% proceed; 50-69% review weak skills and retake with new questions; <50% repeat cluster learning.
After 2 failed attempts on same checkpoint, recommend foundational prerequisite skills before third attempt.
PHASE_END_QUIZ serves as knowledge readiness check alongside project rubrics, timed tests, and mock interviews, not replacing them.
Weight equals difficulty_num (1, 2, 3). Weighted accuracy is sum of weights of correct answers over sum of weights of all questions.
Skill status based on weighted accuracy: STRONG (>=80%), OK (60-79%), WEAK (<60%), requiring at least 2 questions.
When a skill has < 2 questions, compute mastery status at skill_category level (min 3 questions) and mark result as indicative; otherwise UNTESTED.
Untested skills are treated as WEAK for curriculum scheduling purposes but flagged as 'not assessed'.
Weak skills prioritized first; sort by lowest weighted accuracy, then earlier phase_order, then position_in_phase.
A weak skill's weak prerequisites must be scheduled before the dependent skill.
Re-quiz a skill at least 7 days after a WEAK assessment result.
Maintain one 5-question light revision quiz across confirmed skills prior to starting Phase 5.
No duplicate questions within a single quiz; avoid questions seen on the learner's previous attempt for that checkpoint.
If skill x difficulty slot is depleted, use fallback_difficulty_num from File 4; if skill is exhausted, substitute related skills from File 3 with learner disclosure.
Generate synthetic questions matching bank schema when pool has shortfall; flag as GENERATED_UNVERIFIED until programmatic verification (numeric recompute, SQL execution, MCQ position randomization).
Items from the original question bank are the sole items labeled VERIFIED_BANK.
